english.title: Conspire to commit arson with intent to endanger life
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), conspired together with

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSONS..)]_
(C)_[another person]_
(D)_[other persons]_

to commit arson **(..SPECIFY DETAILS..), with intent to endanger life or being reckless as to whether or not life would be endangered
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording document OBSOLETE from 31/12/11. New version at CJS Code CD71003C and H8112.

(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where the damage is to a spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(ii) Property damaged or destroyed may belong to defendant.
(iii) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
